item.text: {"verdict":"request_changes","summary":"The architecture-qualified pin and installer ordering are improved, but four blocking lifecycle/evidence issues and four important specification gaps remain.","recommendations":[{"severity":"blocking","location":"Architecture: the container as the boundary — working tmpfs and lifecycle step 4","issue":"[P1] Docker removes a container's tmpfs mounts when the container stops. The proposed `docker cp` therefore cannot retrieve a verdict written to the working tmpfs from the exited container. The stated stdout fallback is also not a verdict protocol: stdout contains JSONL events, with no specified unambiguous extraction or framing rule.","suggestion":"Keep a wrapper container alive after Codex exits until the runner copies the verdict, use a retained Docker-managed output volume, or define and validate a bounded framing protocol that separates the verdict from JSONL. Preserve the Codex exit status and apply timeout cleanup to the revised lifecycle."},{"severity":"blocking","location":"The credential — capability-enabled controls; Security battery item 1","issue":"[P1] A synthetic dummy `auth.json` cannot authenticate the real model calls needed to make force-enabled shell, web, MCP, app, or plugin controls fire. As written, those controls fail at authentication and cannot generate valid security evidence.","suggestion":"Provide a concrete control-only authentication mechanism, such as a disposable short-lived credential or a host-side authentication broker that never exposes the durable refresh credential. Verify expiry or revocation and demonstrate that each control reaches the real API before accepting its evidence."},{"severity":"blocking","location":"The credential — fresh staging directory; Premises/live-evidence — `container_invocation_profile_hash`","issue":"[P1] The hash is said to cover the full runtime argv, but that argv contains the source path of a fresh staging directory. Its path changes each round, so installer evidence cannot match a subsequent review invocation. Using a stable path would instead introduce concurrency and stale-credential hazards.","suggestion":"Define a canonical semantic invocation profile that replaces validated per-run paths and identifiers with typed placeholders while hashing all security-relevant mount types, destinations, flags, content hashes, ownership/permission constraints, runtime identity, platform, and image identity. Test that fresh equivalent staging paths match and meaningful configuration changes do not."},{"severity":"blocking","location":"Security battery item 2; Architecture — mount/device/socket claims","issue":"[P1] A normal Docker or Podman container's mountinfo never contains only the credential bind and working tmpfs. It also includes the overlay root, procfs, sysfs, cgroups, `/dev`, devpts, shared memory, and runtime-generated mounts such as `/etc/hosts`, `/etc/hostname`, and `/etc/resolv.conf`; standard devices are also present. The literal exact-allowlist assertion will fail on every supported runtime and contradicts the stated host-mount claim.","suggestion":"Specify a runtime-qualified allowlist of required pseudo-filesystems, generated files, devices, mount sources/classes, destinations, and options. Distinguish safe runtime-managed mounts from arbitrary host binds, and continue to reject unexpected devices, sockets, bind sources, and container-runtime sockets."},{"severity":"important","location":"The credential — staging mechanism and container lifecycle","issue":"[P2] The design does not define the staging directory's actual mode, container UID/GID mapping, or read/write mount mode. A fixed non-root image UID may be unable to read or atomically rewrite host-owned files, while refresh generally requires directory write access. It also provides no guaranteed cleanup for the host-side directory containing the copied durable credential.","suggestion":"Define cross-runtime UID/GID and permission handling, including directory-write requirements for atomic refresh, handle-based no-follow copying, a narrowly writable staging mount, cleanup on every outcome, and protected stale-directory recovery after runner crashes."},{"severity":"important","location":"Container lifecycle; Security battery item 4","issue":"[P2] Docker's default logging driver persists container stdout and stderr in daemon-managed host logs. Those logs are an output channel not covered by the listed verdict/JSONL/stderr/diagnostic audit and can survive an interrupted cleanup, undermining the no-disclosure claim.","suggestion":"Disable daemon persistence with a verified logging configuration such as `--log-driver=none` while capturing the attached streams directly, or explicitly collect, audit, bound, permission, and remove runtime logs. Include the effective logging configuration in the invocation fingerprint and battery."},{"severity":"important","location":"The Codex image; Installer step 2","issue":"[P2] The installer permits either building or pulling while requiring a selected child-manifest digest. A normal locally built Docker image has a config/image ID but commonly no registry child-manifest digest, so the required pin cannot be recorded or later resolved by the stated procedure.","suggestion":"Either require pulling an immutable platform child digest, or define an OCI-layout/build-export workflow that deterministically computes and retains the child manifest, verifies its platform and config digest, and executes the corresponding loaded image."},{"severity":"important","location":"Behavioral equivalence requirements; Testing strategy item 4","issue":"[P2] The canonical serialization remains underspecified: “sorted keys,” “unless required,” and “fixed number formatting” do not define the Unicode comparator, escaping and surrogate policy, numeric domains and rendering, negative zero/exponents, normalization, or whether a terminal LF is emitted. A finite golden corpus cannot resolve unspecified inputs.","suggestion":"Adopt a named canonical JSON standard or provide a complete serialization algorithm covering those cases and rejection rules, then make the corpus contain authoritative expected bytes rather than merely comparing the two implementations to each other."}]}
